heroHeadline: 30 Days to Kickoff — Sweden Names Squad; France Announces Tomorrow; Iran Departure to Turkey in 3 Days
heroSubtitle: Sweden became one of the first nations to confirm its final 26-man World Cup squad on May 12, as coach Graham Potter named Viktor Gyökeres (Arsenal), Alexander Isak (Liverpool), and Anthony Elanga in the panel — Victor Lindelöf (75 caps) captaining the side. Roony Bardghji (Barcelona), the 19-year-old prodigy, was controversially left out; Dejan Kulusevski (Tottenham) was also omitted due to injury. Sweden face Tunisia in Monterrey (June 14), the Netherlands in Houston (June 20), and Japan in Dallas (June 25) in Group F. France's Didier Deschamps announces his 26-man squad tomorrow (May 14) in Paris — Kylian Mbappé's hamstring remains the tournament's biggest pre-tournament fitness uncertainty after his exclusion from El Clásico on May 10. Iran's squad is scheduled to depart for a Turkey training camp on May 15 (3 days away) with no US visas yet issued to any Iranian player or coaching staff — whether the departure proceeds will be the next concrete signal of whether the visa standoff is resolving. Iran submitted its provisional squad list by the May 11 FIFA deadline, preserving federation-level participation intent; the FIFA-Taj Zurich meeting (May 20) remains the last formal diplomatic channel before the June 1 final squad deadline. In Mexico, authorities scrapped a proposal to shorten the school year to accommodate World Cup celebrations after public backlash. Squad announcement schedule: New Zealand and France (May 14), Japan (May 15), Brazil (May 18, Ancelotti), Germany (May 21), England (May 22, Tuchel), USMNT (May 26, NYC, FOX Sports). Argentina's final 26-man squad announced May 30; FIFA publishes all 48 squads simultaneously on June 2. 30 days to kickoff at Estadio Azteca.
